title: Falsifiable predictions for the next consented Google Docs live pass
purpose: A prediction recorded after the fact is not a prediction. These numbers are committed BEFORE live pass #2 runs so that the pass can falsify them. testkit/livepass_verify.py grades a fresh gdocs_qualification.json against this file and exits nonzero if the claim below is falsified.

predicts_change.summary: Retire the gdocs per-boundary space_before subtraction.

claim.statement: Google Docs adds ~0pt of vertical space of its own at a flow-element boundary, so a DOCX must emit space_before verbatim.
claim.scope: single-column chunks only; two-column pages excluded because sorting elements by y interleaves the columns and 'consecutive' is undefined there
claim.method: For each pair of consecutive flow elements, gap_delta = dy(first line of el i+1) - dy(last line of el i), measured on Google's own exported PDFs. The file asked for space_before - comp, so Docs' contribution is A = gap_delta + comp. Differencing two dy values cancels the paragraph's internal line-height error; a whole-page regression on cumulative compensation cannot, because there the two are collinear.

competing_model.note: The retired model. Under it, removing the subtraction makes Docs add ~3pt per boundary, so |dy| returns to roughly its pre-fix magnitude. That is what makes the two models separable per document.

outcome.page_match: held on every document that held it before
outcome.note: All five discriminating documents landed inside tolerance and none approached its falsification threshold. The claim is settled, so no document discriminates any more; the entries below are now ordinary regression expectations.

baseline_evidence.name: gdocs-2026-08-04-pass3-qualification.json
baseline_evidence.note: Live pass 3. It confirmed the Noto Serif line-height correction (l1 dy_p50 15.19 -> 1.93) and the cover-band side bleed. It is the run any pass-4 predictions are measured FROM.

superseded_baselines.name: gdocs-2026-08-04-pass2-qualification.json
superseded_baselines.note: Superseded by pass 3. Retained so pass-2 evidence still grades as a baseline rather than a falsification.

superseded_baselines.name: gdocs_qualification.json
superseded_baselines.note: Retained so a pass-1 evidence file still grades as a baseline rather than as a falsification.

prediction_method.name: column-aware counterfactual
prediction_method.description: Every word's measured dy from the 2026-08-04 export, plus the cumulative compensation subtracted above it, reconstructs the drift the uncompensated file would have shown. Cumulative compensation resets at every page break and every ColBreak, because a fresh column starts at the top of the text area regardless of how much space was removed higher up.
assumes: no reflow: pagination and line breaking are unchanged by restoring the space
known_error_sources: half-point font size quantisation moves a baseline up to ~0.5pt per line
the exact->multiple line-height translation has its own residual
restoring ~3pt per boundary adds ~50pt per page on c6_long, which the model does not reflow

tolerance.rationale: The counterfactual is arithmetic, not a re-render. On the least-perturbed document in the corpus (f1_fpdf_brief) the residual |dy| floor is already 1.34pt, and the reflow the model ignores is worth several points on dense pages. A band tighter than this would fail on model error rather than on the claim.

falsification_rule.statement: A-approx-zero is falsified if 2 or more of the discriminating documents exceed their falsifies_A0_above_pt. SETTLED: live pass 2 put all five inside tolerance and none above threshold, so the discriminating set is now empty and this rule can no longer fire.
falsification_rule.threshold_derivation: falsifies_A0_above_pt was the midpoint between the predicted (A=0) and baseline (which A=3 would roughly reproduce in magnitude) dy_p50. Above the midpoint, A~3 explains the observation better than A~0. Only documents whose two hypotheses were separated by >=8pt were allowed to discriminate; the rest were reported without a verdict.
falsification_rule.single_exceedance: warn, do not falsify -- one document can be a reflow artefact
falsification_rule.note: The pass-3 entries below are ordinary regression expectations, not tests of a live claim. The open claims now are font_metric_claim and cover_band_claim, which carry their own falsification terms.

font_metric_claim.statement: Under the gdocs profile, substituting a family whose measured advance width matches the source and tracking out the residual makes Google Docs fit the same number of characters per line as the source producer did.
font_metric_claim.applies_to: l1_word_native (the only corpus document whose mapped family deviates: DejaVu Serif -> Times New Roman, -21.6%)

measured_basis.agreement: 1.5%, on a document where 85 source characters per line became 105

predicted_after.libreoffice_caveat: LibreOffice cannot confirm Docs behaviour and is not offered as evidence of it. It is quoted because it renders the same font files: it measured the BROKEN case at 1.2932 against Google's observed 1.2950, agreeing to 0.14% on advance width specifically, which is the one quantity this fix controls.

font_metric_claim.assumption_requiring_live_verification: That Google Docs renders a run named 'Noto Serif' using the Noto Serif metrics measured here. Noto Serif is Google-authored, is listed in fonts.GDOCS_NATIVE, and Google Fonts ships the file measured -- but the 2026-08-04 export only ever exercised 'Times New Roman', so this is an assumption and not a measurement. If Docs substitutes something else, both the family choice and the computed tracking are wrong together.

falsification.statement: The claim is falsified if l1_word_native's measured packing ratio in the Google export stays above 1.10 -- i.e. the substitution and tracking did not move it materially off the 1.295 it started at.
falsification.how_to_measure: median (characters / line advance width) over full-width body lines of the export, divided by the same quantity on testkit/fixtures/l1_word_native.pdf
falsification.degradation_note: If Docs honours the family but drops w:spacing, the expected packing ratio is 1.067 rather than 1.0018 -- still a large improvement and NOT a falsification. The two mechanisms fail independently by design.

font_metric_claim.status: GRADED against live pass 2 -- NOT falsified, and the degradation branch is the one that happened

outcome.family_assumption: HELD -- the export renders NotoSerif-Regular at 11pt for 862 of 866 body characters, so Docs has the family and used it
outcome.run_tracking: DISCARDED by Docs. 1.0637 sits within 0.3% of the 1.067 predicted for 'family honoured, spacing dropped', and nowhere near the 1.0018 predicted with spacing honoured. fonts.GDOCS_HONOURS_RUN_TRACKING records this and the tracking is retired.
outcome.line_break_evidence: The first body line now wraps identically to the source (85 characters, x 64.9->549.1 against 64.9->550.8) and the paragraph regained its sixth line.
outcome.why_dx_stayed_high: dx_p50 41.76 and dx_p90 345.54 were NOT a packing failure. Substituting Noto Serif without adding its NATURAL_FACTORS entry left the exact->multiple line-height translation dividing by the 1.144 default against Noto Serif's true 1.360, so every line was 19% too tall: the export's pitch was 17.48pt where the source used 14.70. Word matching across vertically displaced lines is what produced the 345pt outliers. Fixing the advance width while breaking the line height traded one drift for another.

line_height_correction.font_file_cross_check: (hhea.ascender - hhea.descender + hhea.lineGap)/unitsPerEm gives 1.362 for Noto Serif, and reproduces the whole existing table with a constant +0.006 offset: Arial 1.150/1.144, Times New Roman 1.150/1.144, Courier New 1.133/1.127, Georgia 1.136/1.130
line_height_correction.predicted_pitch_after: the emitted multiple 0.9833 gives 11 * 1.360 * 0.9833 = 14.71pt against the source's 14.70, a ratio of 1.0007
line_height_correction.guard: tests/test_font_metric_fit.py now requires every substitution candidate to carry a NATURAL_FACTORS entry, so a future family cannot repeat this.

residual_after_pass3.note: Noto Serif is the closest family to DejaVu Serif among those measurable offline AND asserted Docs-native. With tracking discarded by Docs, this 6.3% is currently irreducible and still moves later line breaks within a paragraph, so l1's dx may not reach the 10pt bound on structure alone.
residual_after_pass3.next_step: BUILT: testkit/probe_font_metrics.py, on the ride-along pattern that worked for the cover band. Nine pages, one family each -- Merriweather, Bitter, Libre Baskerville, PT Serif, Lora and IBM Plex Serif as candidates, with Noto Serif, Times New Roman and Georgia as controls that are measurable offline and so validate the round trip. It measures advance width AND natural line height per family, and identifies the rendered face so a family Docs silently substitutes cannot be mistaken for a measurement.

hard_requirements: Docs must have rendered the family itself (no substitution)
its natural line height must have come back, because adopting on advance width alone is what put l1's pitch at 17.48pt against a 14.70pt source
decision_rule.close_the_book_means: no family available to Docs closes the gap; the 6.3% residual is inherent and l1's dx_p50 bound needs a ratified waiver rather than another substitution attempt

residual_after_pass3.libreoffice_control_result: Controls reproduced their offline advances to within 0.12% (Noto Serif -0.09%, Times New Roman -0.10%, Georgia -0.12%) and their natural factors to within 0.011, so the analyzer and the round trip are sound. All six real candidates were substituted by LibreOffice (LiberationSerif), correctly flagged, and correctly excluded from the decision -- which is the failure mode the face check exists to prevent.

pass3_result.status: ANSWERED -- decision ADOPT, pending a writer change and pass-4 verification
pass3_result.docs_has_every_candidate: All nine families rendered natively, 349 of 349 characters each: Merriweather-Regular, Bitter-Regular, LibreBaskerville-Regular, PTSerif-Regular, Lora-Regular, IBMPlexSerif-Regular, plus the three controls. No substitution anywhere.
pass3_result.v1_measurement_was_wrong: The v1 analyzer reported one matched line per family, a nan pitch, and controls drifting +3.57/+4.33/+5.28%. Docs does NOT collapse explicit line breaks -- it preserves them and appends U+200B at each one, so five of six segments failed an exact-text match. The sixth matched but its bounding box carried a trailing space and an 11pt Cambria paragraph mark, which is the whole of the inflation. Merriweather's headline -0.91% was that artefact.
pass3_result.v2_measurement: Word-box extents (first word x0 to last word x1) with zero-width marks stripped, faces counted over visible characters only. All six lines match for every family, pitch is recovered, and controls drift +0.58/+0.78/+0.76% -- systematic at +0.70% with a 0.2% spread, so decide() calibrates candidates on them.
pass3_result.calibration_self_check: Noto Serif calibrates to -6.30% against the -6.18% measured from its own font file, so the calibration is validated by a family whose true value is known independently.
pass3_result.verdict: Libre Baskerville is within 0.04% of DejaVu Serif -- effectively an exact metric match, and far inside the 2% adopt bar. Merriweather is -6.08%, no better than the Noto Serif already in use.

registration_required.note: The advance is the calibrated probe value rescaled onto METRIC_REFERENCE, which is what the rest of FAMILY_METRICS is measured over. Its provenance differs from every other entry -- measured in Docs rather than from a local font file, because Libre Baskerville is not installed here -- and that should be stated where it is written down.

pass3_result.expected_effect: l1_word_native's packing ratio should go from 1.0637 to ~1.000, closing the residual re-wrap that is the last known contributor to its dx_p50 39.82. Needs pass-4 verification.

applied.commit_note: Registered for pass 4 in all three sites, and the substitution rule now picks it for DejaVu Serif on measured distance alone: -0.04% against Noto Serif's -6.29%.

band_gap_claim.status: ledger balanced; probe built and controlled; awaiting its live run in pass 5
band_gap_claim.measurement_note: Everything below is measured on BASELINES, not glyph tops. PyMuPDF derives a span's bbox top from the font's own reported ascender, and 01's source Helvetica reports 1.070-1.075 em where Docs' ArialMT reports 0.905. That is 0.17 x size of apparent drift with the baseline identical -- 1.8pt at 10.5pt and 4.1pt at 25pt. It is why my earlier 'uniform +6.30pt offset' was too large: the true baseline displacement is +3.43 to +5.76, and roughly 1.8pt of 01's dy_p50 8.18 is font metadata rather than misplaced text.

inside_the_band.reading: the band's own content is within 0.6pt; the 14.8pt top compensation and the exact->multiple translation are both working

accumulation_below_it.reading: a further +2.33 accrues down the page, which is the known small line-height residual and not this claim

below_the_band_last_line.requested: tcMar bottom 24.0 + that line's own descent 2.09

step_decomposed.model_accuracy: The same line-box model predicts the band title's baseline to 0.31pt (91.09 predicted against 91.40 measured), so 1.12 and 2.77 are real and not modelling slack.
step_decomposed.balances: 1.12 + 2.77 = 3.89 against the 3.71 measured step, closing to 0.18pt.

families.tcmar: band cell tcMar bottom in {0, 12, 24}pt with space_before fixed -- isolates the 1.12
families.space: following paragraph space_before in {0, 18, 36}pt with tcMar fixed -- isolates the 2.77
families.extra: a spacer paragraph, and a bottom border on the band cell -- the other constructs a cover band can carry
families.plain: no table at all, paragraph to paragraph across the same gap -- the control that says whether the table is implicated

probe_design.reads: band rectangle, the last baseline inside the band, the first baseline after it, and each line's own reported ascent/descent, so a residual is what Docs added beyond what the OOXML asked for

libreoffice_control.resid_bottom: flat at -0.05 across tcMar 0/12/24 -- honoured exactly, and flat means a renderer that adds nothing
libreoffice_control.resid_gap: flat at +0.62 across space_before 0/18/36 -- honoured exactly
libreoffice_control.table_versus_no_table: +0.62 with a table, +0.57 without: LibreOffice adds nothing at a table boundary
libreoffice_control.deliberate_perturbations_detected: the 6pt spacer variant moved the gap by exactly +6.00, and the 1pt bottom border by +1.00
libreoffice_control.reading: every requested quantity is recovered exactly, so any non-flat residual in a Google export is Docs' doing and not the probe's

pass5_must_grade.resid_bottom_flat: If the tcMar family's residual is flat and near +1.1, Docs adds a constant below a band cell regardless of tcMar, and that constant is compensable in the writer.
pass5_must_grade.resid_gap_flat: If the space family's residual is flat and near +2.8, Docs adds a constant at the boundary; if it scales with the request, it is a proportion and needs a different rule.
pass5_must_grade.table_attribution: The plain (no-table) control decides whether either constant belongs to the table boundary or to ordinary paragraph spacing. If the no-table residual matches the banded one, the cover band is not implicated at all and the writer should not gain a band-specific constant.
pass5_must_grade.falsification: If every residual comes back flat near zero -- as LibreOffice's does -- then Docs is honouring the OOXML and the 3.89pt is on the writer's side of the boundary, which would send this back to inference rather than to a gdocs constant.
pass5_must_grade.no_constant_yet: No writer change was made in this chunk. The offline evidence alone does not justify one: it says where the space is, not who adds it.

dy_p50.note: already cleared in pass 3; the family swap changes advance width, and its natural line height is registered, so dy should hold.

dx_p50.reasoning: dx_p50 39.82 has been attributed to re-wrap: with Noto Serif 6.3% narrow, line breaks drifted progressively through each paragraph, and matched words landed on different lines. At a 1.0004 packing ratio the breaks should reproduce the source's, which removes that contributor entirely.
known_residual_contributors: The table cells sit 5.5pt right of source. Measured in pass 1 and deliberately not fixed: the gdocs tcMar relocation (ff518be) removed an accident that had been compensating a table whose true column boundary lies left of the text margin, and reverting it would re-break c7_code. Affects 13 of 141 matched words, so it lifts dx_p90 more than dx_p50.
Half-point font-size quantisation, worth up to ~0.5% of a line's advance.
Residual advance error: Libre Baskerville is -0.04% from DejaVu Serif by the probe's calibrated measurement, whose own controls agree to 0.2%, so call it under 0.3%.
dx_p50.attribution_if_missed: If dx_p50 comes back above ~10 with the packing ratio at ~1.000, the cause is NOT font metrics and the table indent is the only other measured contributor -- which would make it worth reopening rather than the font choice. If the packing ratio itself misses 1.000, the Docs-measured advance for Libre Baskerville is wrong and the probe's calibration needs re-examining, since that number has a different provenance from every other entry in FAMILY_METRICS.

cover_band_claim.statement: Google Docs honours a cover band's side margins exactly, so a true side bleed is reachable by asking for zero; it adds ~14.8pt above a page-leading band unconditionally, so a true top bleed is not.
cover_band_claim.measured_by: testkit/probe_cover_band.py, live pass 2 exploration channel, one variable per page, against a LibreOffice control that honoured all twelve variants exactly

top_family.reading: rendered = requested + ~14.8 throughout. An addition, not a clamp: no requested value reaches the page edge, and asking via header distance lands in the same place (header 14.4 with top 0 differs by 0.43pt).

side_family.reading: relative response tracks requests one-for-one at +2/+4/+8, so side margins are honoured exactly. The constant -24pt x-offset in the raw analyzer output is a coordinate-frame artifact of the probe page geometry, not a Docs behaviour.

changes_made: gdocs cover band asks for a 0pt side margin instead of 4pt, removing a 3.9pt white frame down each edge that was ours, not Google's
cover_band_claim.documented_limitation: ~14.6pt of white above a page-one band is unavoidable in Google Docs. The writer stops trying to beat it: compensation subtracts only where the source left 14.8pt or more, and accepts the floor below that.

pass3_result.side_bleed: LANDED EXACTLY. 01_whitepaper_market's band rendered left 0.00 right 612.00 on a 612pt page, matching the source's 0.00/612.00. Pass 2 was 4.00/607.75, so the 3.9pt white frame down each edge is gone.
pass3_result.top: 14.55pt as measured and as expected; the floor is real and unbeaten.
pass3_result.compensation_was_not_floored: The band's first cover paragraph carried 1068 twips of space_before AFTER the 296-twip subtraction, so 53.4pt remained. The full 14.8pt was applied; this document never hit the floor case.
pass3_result.residual: The band's BOTTOM still lands at 175.05 against the source's 170.00. Docs adds 14.55 above and the writer removes 14.8 inside, which should net to zero, so ~5.05pt of extra height is coming from the band's interior rendering taller than the source's -- a separate effect from the top addition, and not yet attributed.
pass3_result.why_page1_ssim_fell: p1 went 0.6183 (pass 2) -> 0.5996 (pass 3) even though the fix landed. Pass 2's page-1 drift was a SPREAD straddling zero (dy median -2.68, p10 -15.56, p90 +0.14): much of the page was coincidentally aligned. Pass 3's is a single uniform offset (median +6.30, p10 +5.38, p90 +8.36) inherited from the 5.05pt band overhang. A uniform offset overlaps less ink than a spread that crosses zero, so SSIM fell while the document became structurally more correct -- and a single offset is one number to close, where a spread is not.
pass3_result.next_step: Attribute the ~5.05pt of extra band interior height. It is one measurable quantity and closing it should take page 1 from a uniform +6.30pt offset to near zero.

overhang_attributed.verdict: The 'band interior renders taller than the writer accounts' hypothesis is NOT supported. The writer is faithful and Docs' own excess is ~1.4pt, not 5. No gdocs constant is justified, and none was added.
overhang_attributed.the_5pt_was_a_measurement_artefact_of_mi: I had been comparing against the source's DARK rectangle, 0..170. The source's cover block is actually TWO fills: navy 0..170 and a 4pt orange accent bar 170..174. The IR records the block as 174.0 -- correctly -- so the true source bottom is 174.0, not 170.0, and the band overhang is 175.05 - 174.0 = +1.05pt.
overhang_attributed.writer_model_is_faithful: Modelled interior = pads + sum(space_before + space_after + lines*leading) = 173.92 against the IR's 174.0, a 0.08pt agreement. Under this profile a paragraph's rendered line height IS its leading, because the exact->multiple translation emits leading/(size*natural) for Docs to multiply back, so the band is predictable from the layout without rendering anything.
overhang_attributed.docs_side_excess: Requested interior after the 14.8pt subtraction is 159.12, so the predicted bottom is 14.55 + 159.12 = 173.67 against a measured 175.05: Docs delivers ~1.38pt more than asked. Too small, and too close to the glyph-top versus line-box-top ambiguity in these measurements, to encode as a constant.
overhang_attributed.real_defect_found_instead: The 4pt orange accent bar is ABSENT from every Google render, pass 2 and pass 3 alike. Inference represents the two-colour cover block as a single navy cell 174pt tall, so the accent stripe has no representation to emit -- it is not a writer or a Docs problem. Filed separately; it is a visible page-1 fidelity loss independent of any offset.
overhang_attributed.page1_offset_still_open: The uniform +6.30pt offset of page-1 content is therefore NOT explained by the band, which is only 1.05pt low. It originates in the space between the band and the first body element, where the writer emits 36.8pt and the source's visual gap is 34.88pt. Attributing the rest needs a probe rather than more arithmetic on this one document, because the residual is the same size as the glyph-versus-line-box ambiguity.

pass4_prediction.reasoning: Deliberately predicting NO CHANGE. Nothing shipped for pass 4 touches this document: it is Helvetica-based, so the Libre Baskerville substitution does not reach it, and no band constant was added because the evidence did not support one. Predicting an improvement here would be predicting the effect of a change nobody made.

cover_accent_stripe_claim.statement: Re-expressing a cover block's accent stripe as a shaded table row instead of a thick cell border makes Google Docs render it, because Docs honours w:shd cell shading where it drops w:tcBorders at this width.
cover_accent_stripe_claim.applies_to: 01_whitepaper_market (4.0pt orange stripe) and 04_exec_brief (8.0pt indigo stripe) -- the corpus's only two cover accents

corrects_an_earlier_finding.supersedes: cover_band_claim.pass3_result.overhang_attributed.real_defect_found_instead, which recorded that inference 'represents the two-colour cover block as a single navy cell ... it is not a writer or a Docs problem'
corrects_an_earlier_finding.what_inference_actually_does: build_band_table already records a thin flush fill as a border on the band cell. On 01 the cover_band cell carries borders={'bottom': (4.0, '#f59e0b')}, and the writer emits w:tcBorders bottom val=single sz=32 color=F59E0B under BOTH profiles -- w:sz is in eighths of a point, so exactly 4.0pt. The stripe is represented and emitted end to end.
corrects_an_earlier_finding.libreoffice_render_evidence: Sampling the page-1 centre column: the source has ORANGE at y 170..173 (4px); the LibreOffice render-back has ORANGE at y 174..176 under standard and y 159..162 (4px) under gdocs. The construct renders.
corrects_an_earlier_finding.conclusion: The loss is specific to Google Docs. It is a writer/target-translation problem, not an inference gap, and the earlier attribution was wrong.

cover_accent_stripe_claim.why_shading_rather_than_a_border: The navy block is w:shd cell shading on the same cell and comes back in every Docs render, passes 2 through 4, while the stripe never does. Shading is demonstrably honoured by Docs at this geometry where a 4pt table border is not.
cover_accent_stripe_claim.change: docxout._band_accent_as_row, applied only when output_profile == 'gdocs' and only to the cover band: the band becomes two rows -- the original cell with its bottom border removed, and a second row shaded with the accent colour and pinned to the stripe's height.

inference_rule.rule: a full-width fill flush against a band's edge is an accent stripe when it is thin both absolutely and relative to the band
inference_rule.absolute_bound_argument: OOXML stores border width in eighths of a point with a maximum of 96, so a stripe thicker than 12pt cannot be expressed as a border at all
inference_rule.relative_bound_argument: a rule against a block is a small fraction of it; at a quarter of the band's height it is a second band
inference_rule.measured_accents: 4.0pt = 2.4% of its band (01), 8.0pt = 6.2% (04). 8pt is a real accent, so a '<8pt' threshold would have refused one of the two.
inference_rule.refusals_tested: a second large fill (35% of the band), a stripe too thick to be a border (14pt), and a fill that is not flush against either edge

This is deliberately a presence test rather than a score: it is binary, and it cannot be confounded by the page-1 offset that dominates 01's SSIM.
predicted_after.how_to_measure: sample the page-1 raster down its centre column and look for a run of pixels within tolerance of #f59e0b directly beneath the navy run, as testkit's stripe check does offline
predicted_after.secondary_p1_ssim: 0.5996 -> ~0.61. The stripe is 4pt of a 792pt page, so even counting the 8x8 windows it touches it is worth roughly a point of SSIM. The dominant term in 01's page-1 deficit remains the uniform offset, which is a separate workstream.
predicted_after.same_for_04: 04_exec_brief's 8.0pt indigo stripe should appear by the same mechanism; it was never listed as a blocker, so this is a free consequence rather than a claim about its score.

falsification.statement: Falsified if 01's pass-5 page-1 render still has no #f59e0b pixels beneath the navy block. That would mean Docs drops a shaded 4pt table row as well as a 4pt border, and the construct swap is the wrong lever.
falsification.note: A stripe that appears but at the wrong thickness is NOT a falsification of this claim -- it would confirm the construct and move the question to row-height fidelity.

c2_ssim_diagnosis.geometry: dx_p50 0.50, dy_p50 3.88, 48 lines on both sides with identical line breaks -- the words are in the right places

decomposition.best_rigid_shift: dy = -6px (-3.9pt) raises page 1 from 0.6772 to 0.8116, so most of the deficit is a vertical offset rather than content
decomposition.glyph_shape_floor: Liberation Serif against Times New Roman, same text, same size, same position, scores 0.9837 -- they are metric clones with identical advances, so the typeface substitution costs only ~1.6% and is NOT the problem
decomposition.drift_profile: +0.6pt at the title, +2.5 at the abstract, +6.3 at the first two-column heading, +8.1 at the page bottom: a step of roughly 3.8pt at the two-column section boundary, plus ~0.6% per line accumulating within the columns

c2_ssim_diagnosis.why_not_fixed: The step sits in continuous-section and column-start handling, which is the pagination agent's area, and c2's dy_p50 is already inside its bound at 3.88. SSIM at 8x8 windows on dense two-column text simply punishes a sub-4pt offset very hard.

attribution.verdict: LibreOffice-visible. The step is our writer emitting real height at the continuous-section boundary, NOT a Docs-importer artifact, so no gdocs-profile compensation is warranted.
attribution.method: convert c2 under pdfium/gdocs/none/refine0, render with the canonical LibreOffice, match uniquely-identifiable lines to the source and read dy per region
attribution.reproduced_step: abstract lines dy +1.40..+2.10, first two-column heading dy +4.80 -- a step of +3.35pt, against the +3.8pt the live pass measured on the Docs export
attribution.boundary_emits: a spacer paragraph of 13.7pt exact (the hoisted pre_gap), then an empty paragraph carrying the sectPr at w:line=20 exact (1.0pt), then the heading with space_before 16.1pt

experiments.shrink_the_sectpr_paragraph: w:line 20 twips -> 1 twip (1.0pt -> 0.05pt) changed every measured dy by exactly 0.00. LibreOffice ignores lineRule=exact on a paragraph that carries a sectPr and gives it a default line box, so the 'crush' in new_section does nothing.
experiments.remove_the_sectpr_paragraph: folding the sectPr into the preceding spacer's pPr and deleting the empty paragraph moved the heading from +4.80 to -8.90, i.e. -13.70pt. The paragraph occupies about 13.7pt -- a full default line, not the 1pt intended.
experiments.zero_space_before_after_the_break: moved the heading from +4.80 to -11.30, i.e. -16.10pt, exactly the emitted space_before. LibreOffice DOES honour space_before at a continuous-section start, so that is not the missing height.

attribution.why_no_fix_landed: Two errors of opposite sign very nearly cancel here. The sectPr paragraph adds about +13.7pt it should not, yet the net error is only +3.35pt, so something under-emits about 10.35pt at the same boundary and has not been isolated. Removing the sectPr paragraph alone takes c2's heading dy from +4.80 to -8.90 -- larger in magnitude than the 3.88 the document has today. Landing half of a cancelling pair is how a document that is inside its bound leaves it.
attribution.constraint_observed: No code was changed. c2 is a gated fixture and every variant above moves its dy materially, which is a baseline event rather than a silent improvement.
attribution.CORRECTION: The 'cancelling pair' reading above is WRONG and is kept only because the experiment that produced it is on the record. The fold experiment misled: folding the sectPr into the spacer collapses that spacer's own exact height, which is why the heading moved 13.70pt. The section-break paragraph does not occupy 13.7pt. Marker text was put in both paragraphs and read back from the render, and raising the paragraph's w:line from 20 twips to 400 moved every following line down by exactly 19.00pt -- so its height IS honoured, and it costs exactly its w:line, 1.00pt, with a floor near 1pt (which is why 20 -> 1 twip changed nothing). Both boundary errors over-emit; neither cancels the other.

balanced_accounting.measured_on: c2 page 1, pdfium/gdocs/none/refine0, canonical LibreOffice, abstract's last line top to the '1 Introduction' top
balanced_accounting.section_break_paragraph_proof: w:line 20 twips -> 400 moved the heading +19.00pt, exactly the 19pt added; 20 -> 1 twip moved 0.00, the ~1pt floor. It costs its declared 1.00pt and cannot be made to cost less.
balanced_accounting.boundary_arithmetic_detail: _position_chunks sets base = abstract top 133.24 + modelled height 67.50 = 200.74, then pre_gap = target 214.46 - base = 13.70 and the heading's space_before = 230.57 - 214.46 = 16.11, so the emitted gap is 13.70 + 1.00 + 16.10 = 30.80. The abstract's true source bottom is about 204.5 (last line top 191.04 plus leading 13.50), which makes the true gap to the heading about 26.0. _para_box returns height = n * leading measured from a box top that sits ~3pt above the first line's ink top, and c2's abstract pitch is not uniform (13.50, 14.25, 13.50, 13.50), so the modelled bottom lands high and every gap measured from it is that much too large.

resolution.scope: docxout._sect_break_comp returns SECT_BREAK_PARA_PT for output_profile 'gdocs' and 0.0 otherwise, so only the gdocs writer shortens the hoisted gap
resolution.why_by_output_profile_and_not_by_refine_: The standard profile ships with the LibreOffice loop, which has already absorbed this 1pt empirically -- correcting it at source too made the loop over-correct, measured as c2 product-lane mean_ssim 0.824 -> 0.793 and dy_p50 0.85 -> 1.75. The gdocs profile ships with no loop and is the static-translation layer for corrections a loop cannot supply there. Scoping on the output profile rather than on refine_rounds also leaves the raw gate lane alone, because raw runs the standard profile open-loop -- so neither gate lane moves and there is no baseline event.
resolution.standard_unchanged_evidence: word/document.xml sha256 under the standard profile is identical before and after: c2_paper2col 219d901c74d32721, 02_research_paper dd59d9feebbb7793. Those are the only two gated fixtures that emit a hoisted section gap at all.
resolution.gdocs_delta_evidence: under gdocs the hoisted spacer drops by exactly 1.0pt: c2 13.7 -> 12.7 (539d49a20c33c144 -> aa62038d8df6c944), 02 79.1 -> 78.1 (661e6d642f30facf -> 9251b9128fa1eb41)

c2_ssim_diagnosis.pass3_expectation: GRADED and HELD. Nothing shipped for c2 and pass 3 returned mean_ssim 0.6772 with dy_p50 3.88, exactly as predicted.

pass4_expectation.mean_ssim: 0.6772 -> ~0.69. One of the two boundary errors is now corrected on the gdocs path: 1.00pt of the measured 3.30pt over-emission. The raw-lane LibreOffice proxy moved +0.016 for exactly this 1.00pt, and that is the whole basis for the number -- it is an extrapolation from one renderer to another, not a measurement of Docs.
pass4_expectation.dy_p50: ~3.88, essentially UNCHANGED, and that is expected rather than a disappointment. dy_p50 is a median over 48 matched lines; correcting 1.00pt of a 3.30pt boundary step moves the lines below the boundary by 1pt and leaves the lines above it alone, which barely moves a median. SSIM is the metric this claims, because SSIM punishes the offset everywhere it appears.
pass4_expectation.falsification: The claim is falsified if c2's mean_ssim comes back below 0.68 -- i.e. the correction did not move it materially off the 0.6772 it has held for two passes. A value at or above 0.70 would mean it helped more than the LibreOffice proxy predicted.
pass4_expectation.caveat: The remaining 2.30pt is untouched, so c2 stays well short of the 0.8116 that removing the whole offset demonstrates, and well short of its 0.70 bound being comfortably cleared.

c2_ssim_diagnosis.next_step: TASK #20, not this chunk: the remaining 2.30pt. It lives in _position_chunks working from a paragraph bottom that _para_box places too high, and closing it is a wider change than this boundary -- _para_box sets every paragraph's space_before in every document, so it moves the whole corpus and both gate lanes rather than one profile's section boundaries.

checks.description: The five documents whose dy_p50 blocker this fix is meant to clear must land within tolerance of prediction AND under the 10.0pt bound.

c1_whitepaper is predicted at 10.44 against a 10.0 bound. Report which side it lands on; a miss here is model error, not falsification, because its page 2 matched only 32 words at dy -55 (suspected pagination effect).
Restoring ~3pt per boundary adds roughly 50pt per page on c6_long. The counterfactual does not simulate reflow, so page_match must be confirmed on every multi-page document.

c2_paper2col mean_ssim should rise from its pre-fix 0.6532 as its dy collapses from 23.01 to a predicted 3.53. This is the least-supported prediction in the set: two-column pages were excluded from the boundary measurement.

Documents where the subtraction was accidentally cancelling genuine positive drift. These are PREDICTED to get worse; worsening here confirms the model rather than contradicting it. All must stay under the 10.0pt bound.

01_whitepaper_market mean_ssim should rise, driven by pages 2 and 3. Page 1 should NOT materially improve: its 0.6183 is dominated by the cover band, which Google renders 14.4pt below the page top with a 3.9pt white frame, and that floor is untouched by this change.

l1_word_native's dx_p50 was 63.65pt, driven entirely by re-wrap: Times New Roman is 21.6% narrower than the source's DejaVu Serif, so 85 characters per line became 105 and matched words landed on different lines. With the family substituted to Noto Serif and the residual tracked out, the re-wrap should be gone and dx must come inside the 10.0pt bound. A dx still in the tens of points means the substitution did not take effect in Docs.

Separately measured and deliberately NOT fixed: l1's table cells render 5.5pt right of source because the gdocs tcMar relocation (ff518be) removed an accident that was compensating a table whose true column boundary sits left of the text margin. It is inside the bound, affects 13 of 141 matched words, and reverting it would re-break c7_code. Reported so it is not mistaken for a font-fit failure.
